title: Allow direct commits on a core branch from bootstrap.toml

keeps.check: From the run worktree, resolve the pre-commit binary with mise x -- which pre-commit, and prepend its folder to PATH so that mise x -- which pre-commit also finds it in a folder without a mise config. Make a temporary git repository with the branches main and develop, and check out develop. Copy tools/mise/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/helpers and tools/mise/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/checks of the worktree into its .config/mise/tasks/_scripts/, and write a minimal .config/pre-commit-config.yaml that holds only the pre-commit/pre-commit-hooks repo (rev v6.0.0) with the no-commit-to-branch hook and args ["--branch", "main", "--branch", "develop"]. Commit all three files, so the tree is clean. From the temporary repository, with MISE_PROJECT_ROOT set to it, run precommit_safety_net twice in fresh shells: first after sourcing the merge library of the branch base (git show <base>:tools/git/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/merge), then after sourcing the changed tools/git/.config/mise/tasks/_scripts/merge. pre-commit may fetch the hook repo over the network or use its cache. No remote and no push.
keeps.pass: The base library returns non-zero and the changed library returns 0, and neither run prints "pre-commit is not on PATH" or "No .config/pre-commit-config.yaml", so both runs really ran the hooks.

decisions.decision: Does this plan finish B13 or land one piece of it?
decisions.ruling: Finish B13. The plan lands the key, the validation, the render, the tests and the docs. The user does the macos-setup change by hand after the landing.
decisions.rejected: Land a piece of B13 and keep the macos-setup step open on a Parked line.

decisions.decision: Which combinations of direct_commit are valid?
decisions.ruling: One core branch, either main or develop, depending on the repo's need: direct_commit on that branch drops it from the hook, and with no branch left the sync removes the hook. With both main and develop: develop only (the hook keeps --branch main), or both (the sync removes the hook). User: "There can never be a situation where main is allowed for direct-commit but develop is NOT." That case stops the sync with code 2.
decisions.rejected: Any combination, with no rule between the branches.

decisions.decision: How must the merge safety net treat no-commit-to-branch?
decisions.ruling: The safety net always runs with SKIP=no-commit-to-branch. The hook guards a commit, and the safety net does not make a commit; a merge never runs the hook, because the hook types do not include pre-merge-commit.
decisions.rejected: Skip the hook only when the source branch is protected; a flag of code:merge:main that skips it.

decisions.decision: What is the shape of the new key, and who validates it?
decisions.ruling: A boolean direct_commit in [branch.main] and [branch.develop]. repo-sync validates it before it writes any file, in the same step as _rs_mise_env and _rs_overrides: a non-boolean value, the key in any other [branch.*] table, and main true without develop true when both branches exist each stop the sync with code 2. The merge tasks do not read the key.
decisions.rejected: One top-level list direct_commit = ["develop"]; one mode for each repository ("none", "develop", "all").

decisions.decision: What does the sync do with direct_commit for a core branch that the repository does not have?
decisions.ruling: It stops the sync with code 2. The message names the table and says that the branch does not exist.
decisions.rejected: Log a warning and continue; ignore it with no message.

decisions.decision: What do the name and the description of the hook say after the change?
decisions.ruling: Neutral fixed text, for example "Refuse a direct commit to a protected branch". The --branch args show which branches the hook protects.
decisions.rejected: Render the branch names into the name.

decisions.decision: Where does the sync change the args of the hook?
decisions.ruling: In repo-sync, where _rs_context builds .precommit: find the hook with the id no-commit-to-branch, remove each --branch <b> pair whose branch has direct_commit = true, and remove the hook when no branch is left. The template does not change. Accepted: a no-commit-to-branch hook in the consumer file .config/repo-sync/pre-commit.yaml changes the same way.
decisions.rejected: Change the args in the loop over the hooks of the pre-commit template.

decisions.ruling: Add direct_commit to the examples where it fits, review all the examples against the contract commits since commit_id (git log <commit_id>..HEAD -- tools docs/sync CLAUDE.md), and set commit_id. The gates unit sets commit_id last, so no contract commit of the plan comes after it.
decisions.rejected: Add the key only and park the full review; do not change the examples.

decisions.decision: How does B14 relate to this plan?
decisions.ruling: B14 is a separate plan that requires this one, planned next in the same session.
decisions.rejected: Include B14 in this plan; leave B14 in the backlog.

decisions.decision: Does the plan need a review unit?
decisions.ruling: Yes. U1 and U2 change shell scripts that run: the merge library and repo-sync. One review unit in wave 2 covers U1, U2 and U3.
decisions.rejected: No review unit; the wave review only.

decisions.decision: How does the docs unit make sure that the docs are correct?
decisions.ruling: All four parts: (1) the explicit list of passages in 05-docs.md, each with its change; (2) then vwf:docs-sync over the full branch delta, with a fix for each passage it finds that the list does not name; (3) a grep check: no doc names the old hook text "main or develop", and each listed file that describes the key has a hit for direct_commit; dprint check over the docs; (4) the examples stay a separate unit (U3). The unit also adds one optional M<n> item to docs/sync/migrate.md.

decisions.decision: How do the examples show the key?
decisions.ruling: Assumed: as a commented line under [branch.develop], with one comment line that gives the rule, so that a consumer who copies an example does not allow direct commits by accident. Only polyrepo-develop and monorepo get the line. No other example gets it, and no example shows it in [branch.main].
decisions.rejected: A real (not commented) key in the examples.

decisions.decision: Is direct_commit = false validated like true?
decisions.ruling: Yes. The sync validates the key when it is present, whatever its value: false in a table other than [branch.main] or [branch.develop], and false for a core branch that does not exist, each stop the sync with code 2. false has no effect on the render.
decisions.rejected: Treat false as no key everywhere.

decisions.decision: Which forms of a consumer no-commit-to-branch hook does the sync change?
decisions.ruling: Only --branch <b> pairs, the form of the git tool. A hook with no args, or with --branch=<b> or -b <b>, stays as it is. The sync removes a hook that had --branch pairs and has none left, also when it has other args: with no --branch arg, no-commit-to-branch of pre-commit-hooks v6.0.0 protects main and master by default.
decisions.rejected: Also match --branch=<b> and -b <b>; drop a hook with no args; keep a hook with its other args when its --branch pairs are gone (it then protects main and master by default).

decisions.decision: Does the sync drop the --branch pair of a core branch that does not exist?
decisions.ruling: Yes. The render drops the --branch <b> pair of each core branch (main, develop) that _rs_branch_exists does not find, and of each branch with direct_commit = true. So the hook protects only the core branches that exist and do not allow direct commits, and a one-branch repo with direct_commit on that branch has no hook (D2). Side effect, accepted: each one-branch consumer gets --branch <its branch> only at its next sync, with no new key; a new develop branch comes back at the sync after it exists.
decisions.rejected: Drop pairs only for direct_commit = true, and change D2 so that a one-branch repo keeps the hook for the missing branch.
